text:
Vincent Trocheck is a Pittsburgh kid now centering a Pittsburgh line in Salt Lake City. After six games with the Rangers this season he landed in Utah, and the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette noticed that the Mammoth have paired him with Logan Cooley, another Pittsburgh native. Eleven games in, the fit looks good on process: Utah gets about 60% of the 5v5 chances with Trocheck on the ice, better than it does without him, and he is getting more dangerous looks per 60 minutes than he did last season.

The points have lagged a bit. He has ten in 17 games, three goals on about four goals' worth of chances, and his teammates are finishing a couple of goals below what their chances deserve with him out there. Both of those tend to even out. He has always been more passer than finisher, and Evolving-Hockey noted he drew the toughest competition in the league last season, which also came with a cost in his own end. Our projection has him around 53 points, right where he finished last year. If the Cooley pairing holds, the assists should start arriving in bunches.
headline: Trocheck finds a home on a Pittsburgh line in Utah
